questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of Complex Fourier Form?
questions.answer: The complex Fourier form uses exponentials instead of separate sine and cosine terms. It is compact, symmetric in positive and negative harmonics, and natural for waves and signal spectra.

questions.prompt: State a central formula or test for Complex Fourier Form.
questions.answer:
The complex fourier series is
\[f(x)\sim\sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}c_ne^{inx}\]
Use it only after the symbols in the formula have been identified for the specific complex fourier form problem.

questions.prompt: How is the formula or method in Complex Fourier Form interpreted rather than just memorised?
questions.answer:
Interpret the symbols and the condition being tested. The complex coefficient is
\[c_n=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)e^{-inx}\,dx\]
Use it only after the symbols in the formula have been identified for the specific complex fourier form problem.

questions.prompt: Show why c_n is found by multiplying by e to the negative i n x and integrating.
questions.answer: Start with \[f(x)=\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty}c_me^{imx}\] Multiply by e^{-inx}: \[f(x)e^{-inx}=\sum_{m=-\infty}^{\infty}c_me^{i(m-n)x}\] Integrate over negative pi to pi. Orthogonality gives \[\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}e^{i(m-n)x}\,dx=2\pi\] when m=n and zero otherwise. Therefore \[\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)e^{-inx}\,dx=2\pi c_n\] so \[c_n=\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)e^{-inx}\,dx\]

questions.answer: The terms e^{inx} and e^{-inx} represent opposite phase directions in complex notation. A real signal combines conjugate coefficients so the imaginary parts cancel in the final real function. This makes wave and signal spectra easier to organise.
